blocks.title: Mathematics · compare whole numbers and decimals
blocks.notes: Brief rounding review: 7.264 to hundredths is 7.26. Introduce comparison, rather than assuming it is already taught. Model 4,582 > 4,528: thousands and hundreds match; compare tens, 8 > 2. Align place values and compare left to right. Model 4.70 > 4.65: ones match; 7 tenths > 6 tenths. Practice: 4,209 < 4,290; 6.4 > 6.04; 2.5 = 2.50; 0.63 < 0.7. Explain the deciding place. Exit: explain 6.08 < 6.8. Booklets A/B page 1 offer number choices; English–Korean packet page 1 provides a bilingual comparison model. Choose appropriate questions, not all sheets.
blocks.firstAction: Round 7.264 to the nearest hundredth, then compare 4,582 and 4,528.
studentSteps: Compare from the greatest place value; stop at the first different digit.
Try a pair, explain the deciding place to a partner, then complete one independent comparison.
blocks.firstActionKo: 7.264를 소수 둘째 자리까지 반올림한 뒤 4,582와 4,528의 크기를 비교하세요.

blocks.title: English Language Arts · Nevermoor
blocks.notes: Confirm the actual class bookmark before reading; do not assume a chapter. Choose a short section and listen for what a character wants, feels or thinks. Model an idea plus a detail from this reading, then explain how the detail supports the idea. Students write, draw, say or dictate a brief response and a question. Record the stopping point. English–Korean packet page 5 provides a matching response page.
blocks.firstAction: Recall the last part we actually heard, or listen to the opening.
studentSteps: Listen for a character or setting detail.
Write, draw or say an idea and the detail that supports it.
Keep one question for our next reading.
blocks.firstActionKo: 지난번에 들은 마지막 부분을 떠올리거나 이야기의 시작 부분을 들으세요.

blocks.title: Social Studies and Language Arts · fair communities
blocks.notes: Ask: What makes a community fair, and what would we improve? Begin with a shared-space example: one group uses a play area every recess. Model a possible improvement, who it affects and what still needs checking; different defensible solutions are welcome. Students choose a public issue, identify affected people and suggest a decision plus who could help make it. Use the community reflection to write or dictate a paragraph with a reason and an inquiry question. Partners identify a clear reason; revise one sentence when feedback helps. Booklets A/B page 2 and English–Korean packet page 2 offer alternative routes.
blocks.firstAction: Think of a shared place or rule. Who can take part, and what could improve?
studentSteps: Choose a public issue and identify who is affected.
Explain one possible improvement, who could help decide, and a question to investigate.
Write or dictate a short paragraph. Share a reason with a partner and make a useful revision.

blocks.title: ADST and Language Arts · Bloxels paper planning
blocks.notes: Use paper today. Model a character who wants to cross a river: a broken bridge creates the obstacle; the player can repair it or find another route. Discuss how the choice changes the story. Partners plan character, setting, goal, obstacle and one small level with a start and goal. Each student writes their own 3–5 sentence opening, or uses an oral, drawn or dictated route. Booklets A/B pages 3–5 and English–Korean pages 3–4 offer alternatives. Build a small part during the next suitable Tuesday or Thursday technology block; exact booking times are unconfirmed.

studentSteps: Plan a character, setting, goal and problem with your partner.
